Sam: Quick summary — I ran perf + nsys on the prefetch/batching patch (branch: pref-batch-coord). Seeing CPU spikes dominated by BatchCoordinator::dispatch_loop and Tokenizer::token_split. KV cache invalidation also spikes when prefetcher hits a stale prefix.

Maria: Can you paste the perf top/flame? link?

Sam: Pulling snippet from perf flame (collapsed stack):
```
  23.4% BatchCoordinator::dispatch_loop
  12.8% Tokenizer::token_split
   9.0% PyEval_EvalFrame
   6.5% memcpy
   4.2% std::function<>::operator()
```
Full flamegraph uploaded: https://s3.redwood-internal/perf/2134567890/prefetch-flame.svg :eyes:

Cheng: Huh — memcpy and std::function smell like the kernel selection path is copying small tensors for fallback kernels. Did you see any vmmap/kernel-switch syscall churn in the nsys trace? nvtx marks show a handful of kernel fallbacks around sequence length 36.

Sam: nsys summary:
- 6 fallback launches inside 200ms window
- avg kernel launch latency +1.8ms during those
- cpu-side: BatchCoordinator holds a spinlock for ~200us per dispatch
Attached nsys timeline: https://s3.redwood-internal/perf/2134567890/nsys-timeline.qdrep

Natalie: Could be two things: (1) kernel threshold tuning causing small-batch kernels to be selected frequently, (2) Python glue allocating temporaries while deciding kernel. Try bumping kernel_selector::min_tokens_for_fast_kernel from 32->48 and re-run.

Sam: Did a quick local experiment — setting threshold to 48 reduced the number of fallbacks by ~75% and CPU time in memcpy dropped ~60%. Here's the tiny patch I used:
```
- constexpr int MIN_FAST_KERNEL_TOKENS = 32;
+ constexpr int MIN_FAST_KERNEL_TOKENS = 48;
```

Maria: Nice. Any regression on latency P50/P95?

Sam: P50 stable, P95 improved slightly (because we avoided a few slow fallback launches). We'll run a canary with real traffic.

Cheng: Also look at Tokenizer path — Tokenizer::token_split spikes on inputs with lots of emoji/unicode. Consider caching tokenization for repeated prefixes (prefix KV) and avoid re-parsing inside dispatch loop.

Sam: Good call. We saw KV cache churn: prefetcher invalidates a small prefix when it prefetches next token window. I think we can decouple prefetch invalidation from dispatch by moving invalidation to prefetch completion path (so dispatch reads from stable cache snapshot).

Natalie: If you open a short PR with the threshold change + perf numbers I'll run it against canary infra tomorrow AM. Add a benchmark job (perf/regress.prefetch) so we catch regressions.

Sam: Will do. Creating PR now and will attach perf logs. Thanks all :raised_hands:

InfraBot: nsys run queued on perf-runner-5 for job 2134567890-prefetch-canary

Maria: Great, assigning Cheng to follow tokenization caching follow-up. :memo:

Sam: Updated participants — leaving logs in the PR and will ping when canary completes.
